capabilities.target: vendor master record, including bank details

inputs.source: Supplier invoice uploaded to the supplier portal

instructions.note: The only safeguard against a fraudulent bank-detail change is a prompt-level instruction to 'request approval with a one line summary.' There is no instruction or structural requirement to verify new bank details out of band before updating the vendor record.

'If the invoice shows new bank details, update the vendor record' treats content from an untrusted, externally-submitted invoice as sufficient basis to modify sensitive vendor master data, granting the invoice implicit authority over payment routing.

controls.name: Clerk approval card before payment or bank change
controls.decay_rationale: The approver sees only a model-generated one-line summary; bank account numbers and change history are never shown, so the gate cannot catch a fraudulent bank change even today. A more persuasive model under model_upgrade, combined with ~150 cards/day of approval volume, erodes it further (ASI09, SAFE-T1403).

controls.name: Bank destination confirmation bound to system of record
controls.decay_rationale: A comparison of the new bank details against the previously stored value, or an independent out-of-band verification, is enforced against the system of record rather than model output, so it would not decay with model capability.

controls.name: Least-privilege ERP credential scoping
controls.decay_rationale: A credential scoped to specific vendors or POs rather than 'any vendor, any payment' does not decay with model capability, since the model cannot use access it does not have.

controls.name: Documented review gate on model upgrades
controls.decay_rationale: A governance checkpoint requiring sign-off before swapping the underlying model does not itself decay with capability; it controls whether the forecast trigger can occur silently.

findings.title: Invoice-driven vendor bank-account takeover and fraudulent payment, gated only by a blind, fatigue-prone approval summary (confused deputy / TC4, ASI09)

attack_path.note: Attacker submits an invoice through the supplier portal containing new bank details for an existing vendor.
Agent reads the vendor master record to match the invoice to a vendor and PO.
Agent updates the vendor's bank details based on invoice content (untrusted input), using a broadly-scoped credential.
Clerk sees only a one-line model summary; bank account numbers and prior value are never shown, so the change cannot be judged on its merits.
Agent schedules payment to the now-updated, attacker-controlled bank account; funds transfer is irreversible.

findings.residual_rationale: The rubric's step-2 floor for a model_summary approval gate is moderate, but runtime notes confirm the approval card never displays the bank account number or the prior value for bank-detail changes. The approver cannot detect the fraud indicator even when the model's summary is entirely accurate. This is a present-day structural blind spot in what the gate surfaces, not only a capability-driven persuasion risk, so residual is held at high rather than the formulaic moderate floor.

evidence.observation: Instructs the agent to update vendor bank details from invoice content and to gate payment/bank changes on a one-line approval summary only.
The card shown to the clerk displays only payee, amount, invoice id, and PO match; it does not display any bank account information or indicate that bank details changed.
"Bank account numbers and the change history are not shown." confirms the approver structurally cannot evaluate the riskiest fact.
"The ERP credential can update any vendor and schedule any payment." confirms credential_scope broad, no least-privilege containment.
"The clerk approves roughly 150 cards per day" and "The model is upgraded with the platform, with no separate review" together establish the approval-fatigue and model_upgrade forecast triggers.

forecast.watch_signal: Model version or platform model string changes without a documented review event, while approval volume stays near ~150 cards/day/reviewer and the clerk's approve rate trends toward ~100% (approval fatigue).

recommendations.action: Require destination confirmation bound to the system of record: before scheduling any payment, verify the destination bank account against the value on file prior to the invoice-triggered change, or require independent out-of-band verification (phone call to a known contact, not one supplied by the invoice).

Change the approval review mode for bank-detail changes and payments from model_summary to raw_action: show the approver the old and new bank account numbers, the requester/source document, and change history.
Scope the ERP credential to least privilege (vendors tied to open POs, payment caps) instead of 'any vendor, any payment.'
Require two-person or specialist review for bank-detail changes specifically, separate from routine payment approval, to counter approval fatigue at ~150 cards/day.
Log and alert on any bank-detail change followed by a payment within a short window; compare new bank details against known-fraud indicators.
Require a documented review before the underlying model is upgraded, since it is currently swappable with no separate review.

rating.rationale: Untrusted invoice content can drive a vendor bank-detail change (restricted data) followed by an irreversible outbound payment (spend, S3), giving inherent risk critical (U source x S3 sink). The only control is a human approval gate; its model_summary review mode would ordinarily floor residual at moderate, but runtime notes confirm it never shows the bank account number or change history, a present-day structural blind spot rather than only a capability-driven weakness, so residual is held at high. Under the model_upgrade trigger (the model is swappable with no separate review), the gate's already-weak protection fails further, and with no other preventive control in place (no destination confirmation, no scoped credential, no raw-action review), the finding reverts to the unmitigated critical tier in forecast.

limitations: This assessment reflects declared design and configuration as described in the provided artifacts (prompt.md, the approval card mock, and runtime notes), not observed runtime behavior.

No tool manifest, MCP config, or IaC was provided; capability credential scope is inferred from the runtime-notes narrative ('can update any vendor and schedule any payment') rather than a verified policy document, so confidence on the exact scope boundary is medium even though overall finding confidence is high.

It is not confirmed whether the approval card's one-line summary format is identical for bank-detail-change approvals and payment approvals; the single example shown is for a payment. This is treated conservatively as equally blind to bank-detail changes, consistent with the runtime note that account numbers and change history are never shown.
